findings.control_name: No Public S3 Bucket Read
findings.control_description: S3 buckets must not allow public read access. Detects buckets with anonymous read exposure via policy or ACL.

evidence.temporal_risk: Asset non-compliant for 240 hours (SLA: 0 hours). Exposed since 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.

remediation.description: Bucket has public read access enabled via policy or ACL. Anyone on the internet can access objects in this bucket.
remediation.action: Enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove any bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove any ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.

preconditions: Confirm resource ownership and internal change window approval.
Ensure public access is not explicitly required for this specific resource's function.
fix_plan.expected_effect: Enforces a hardened security posture by blocking all identity-bound and resource-bound public access paths.
fix_plan.action: Enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove any bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove any ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.

violation.control_name: No Public S3 Bucket Read

reasoning.clause: the bucket allows anonymous read = true

remediation_context.action: Enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove any bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove any ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.

findings.defect: The bucket's access configuration grants read permission to the public — either via a bucket policy statement with Principal "*" or via an ACL grant to the AllUsers pseudo-group. The bucket is reachable without authentication from the public internet.
findings.infection: Anyone on the internet can fetch objects from this bucket over anonymous HTTP/HTTPS. Search engines and automated scanners continuously enumerate publicly-indexed bucket names, meaning exposure is active from the moment the policy or ACL is in place — not hypothetical. Once the bucket name is known, every object whose key the caller can guess or enumerate is fetchable.
findings.failure: Unbounded data exposure. Every file stored in this bucket is readable by arbitrary internet callers, including potentially sensitive operational data, customer information, backup artifacts, or internal documentation that wasn't intended to reach the public surface.

findings.control_name: No Public S3 Buckets With Sensitive Data
findings.control_description: S3 buckets tagged with sensitive data classifications (PHI, PII, confidential) must not allow any public access.

evidence.temporal_risk: Asset non-compliant for 240 hours (SLA: 0 hours). Exposed since 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.

remediation.description: A bucket containing sensitive data (PHI, PII, or confidential) has public read or list access. This data is accessible to anyone on the internet.
remediation.action: Immediately enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers. Audit CloudTrail logs for unauthorized access during the exposure window.

preconditions: Confirm resource ownership and internal change window approval.
Ensure public access is not explicitly required for this specific resource's function.
fix_plan.expected_effect: Enforces a hardened security posture by blocking all identity-bound and resource-bound public access paths.
fix_plan.action: Immediately enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers. Audit CloudTrail logs for unauthorized access during the exposure window.

violation.control_name: No Public S3 Buckets With Sensitive Data

reasoning.clause: the bucket allows anonymous list = true
the bucket allows anonymous read = true

remediation_context.action: Immediately enable S3 Public Access Block (all four settings). Remove bucket policy statements granting access to Principal "*". Remove ACL grants to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers. Audit CloudTrail logs for unauthorized access during the exposure window.

findings.defect: A bucket tagged with a sensitive-data classification (PHI, PII, or confidential) is exposed via public read or public list. The tag declares the data's sensitivity; the access state contradicts that declaration.
findings.infection: Any internet caller can fetch the sensitive objects via anonymous GET or enumerate them via anonymous ListBucket. Search engines and compliance scanners specifically match data-classification tags against access state, so a single tagged-sensitive + public bucket becomes the highest-priority finding in most posture dashboards. Regulators treat the classification tag as evidence of awareness: the organization has labeled this data sensitive and nonetheless exposed it publicly, which weakens claims of accidental oversight.
findings.failure: Regulated-data breach. PHI exposure triggers HIPAA breach notification; PII exposure triggers GDPR/CCPA obligations; confidential data exposure typically triggers contractual disclosure and customer notification. Remediation scope is bounded by the exposure window — audit CloudTrail to bound who accessed during that window and produce the notification roster.

findings.control_name: Anonymous S3 Listing Must Be Explicitly Intended
findings.control_description: Anonymous bucket listing increases exposure surface even when objects are public by design. Listing must be explicitly intended via tag.

evidence.temporal_risk: Asset non-compliant for 240 hours (SLA: 0 hours). Exposed since 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.

remediation.description: Bucket has public listing enabled without an explicit intent tag. Anonymous listing increases exposure surface even for public content.
remediation.action: If listing is intentional, add the tag public_list_intended=true to the bucket. Otherwise, remove the policy or ACL granting s3:ListBucket to Principal "*" or AllUsers.

preconditions: Confirm resource ownership and internal change window approval.
Ensure public access is not explicitly required for this specific resource's function.
fix_plan.expected_effect: Enforces a hardened security posture by blocking all identity-bound and resource-bound public access paths.
fix_plan.action: If listing is intentional, add the tag public_list_intended=true to the bucket. Otherwise, remove the policy or ACL granting s3:ListBucket to Principal "*" or AllUsers.

violation.control_name: Anonymous S3 Listing Must Be Explicitly Intended

reasoning.clause: the bucket allows anonymous list = true
the bucket's public-list-intended tag is not set
the bucket's public-list-intended tag not equal "true" (observed: not set)

remediation_context.action: If listing is intentional, add the tag public_list_intended=true to the bucket. Otherwise, remove the policy or ACL granting s3:ListBucket to Principal "*" or AllUsers.

findings.defect: The bucket grants s3:ListBucket to an anonymous or wildcard principal (public_list = true) without the public_list_intended tag set to true. The catalog treats intentional listing as acceptable (for software download mirrors, archives, and documented-public catalogs) — absence of the tag means listing is almost certainly unintended.
findings.infection: Anonymous callers can enumerate every object key in the bucket via a single API call. Enumeration is the step attackers most often lack when objects themselves are publicly readable but unlisted — without a key, a plain public-read bucket is safer than its ACL suggests. Public list removes that obscurity, converting "attackers must guess keys" into "attackers pull the manifest." Automated scanners specifically enumerate bucket contents via list-bucket and archive the manifest even if individual objects are not immediately readable.
findings.failure: Catalog exfiltration. Every object's key, size, modification time, and (often) content hash becomes attacker-known. If some objects are additionally public-readable, those become mass-harvestable via list-then-get. If objects are not public-readable, the manifest still discloses data- classification metadata (filenames often reveal sensitivity), business operations (backup cadence, batch-job naming), and organizational structure (folder layouts mirroring team hierarchies).

delta.fix_action: populate this property in the configuration

findings.control_name: No Public Read via Bucket Policy
findings.control_description: S3 bucket policies must not grant read access to an anonymous or wildcard principal. A Statement with Effect Allow, Principal "*" or AWS: "*", and an Action such as s3:GetObject without a restricting Condition enables any unauthenticated caller to read objects. This is distinct from CTL.S3.PUBLIC.001, which fires on the composite public_read signal regardless of mechanism; this control narrows to the bucket-policy path so the finding points the operator at the policy specifically. For ACL-based public read, see CTL.S3.ACL.FULLCONTROL.001 (FULL_CONTROL grants) and CTL.S3.ACL.ESCALATION.001 (WRITE_ACP grants).

evidence.temporal_risk: Asset is currently in a non-compliant state.

remediation.description: Bucket policy grants s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAcl, or equivalent read action to an anonymous or wildcard principal. Any unauthenticated caller can read objects.
remediation.action: Remove or constrain the policy statement granting read actions to Principal "*" or AWS: "*". If broad read access is genuinely required, add a restricting Condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpc, or a fixed aws:SourceIp CIDR. Enable S3 Public Access Block with BlockPublicPolicy set to true to reject future policies that grant public read.

preconditions: Confirm resource ownership and internal change window approval.
Ensure public access is not explicitly required for this specific resource's function.
fix_plan.expected_effect: Enforces a hardened security posture by blocking all identity-bound and resource-bound public access paths.
fix_plan.action: Remove or constrain the policy statement granting read actions to Principal "*" or AWS: "*". If broad read access is genuinely required, add a restricting Condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpc, or a fixed aws:SourceIp CIDR. Enable S3 Public Access Block with BlockPublicPolicy set to true to reject future policies that grant public read.

violation.control_name: No Public Read via Bucket Policy

reasoning.clause: the bucket policy grants read to a public principal = false

remediation_context.action: Remove or constrain the policy statement granting read actions to Principal "*" or AWS: "*". If broad read access is genuinely required, add a restricting Condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:SourceVpc, or a fixed aws:SourceIp CIDR. findings.defect: The bucket policy contains a Statement with Effect "Allow", Principal "*" (or AWS: "*"), and a read action such as s3:GetObject or s3:GetObjectAcl. No restricting Condition narrows the principal to a specific account, VPC, IP range, or organization.

findings.infection: PAB is a defense-in-depth control: even if the bucket is currently private, any subsequent change to the bucket policy or ACL can make it public with no intermediate warning. PAB, when fully enabled, rejects the change at configuration time — the AWS API returns an error rather than accepting the unsafe policy. Without PAB, operators performing routine maintenance or automation running at scale can accidentally flip a bucket public. Audit trails attribute the exposure to the operator or script, not to the absent safety net, so investigations often miss that PAB-on-everywhere would have prevented the incident.
findings.failure: Future accidental exposure through routine bucket changes. The bucket is not currently public, so this control is preventive, not reactive — the failure it describes is whatever would happen if an unrelated configuration change made the bucket public. Enabling PAB eliminates the class entirely for this bucket regardless of which mechanism (ACL, policy, future API surface) would otherwise have opened the exposure.
